Control Objective: Risk appetite and tolerance statements are established, communicated and maintained.
Relevance to This Incident: Hot-wallet exposure is the firm's largest single appetite decision; ~$6.34-6.43B was reachable through one signing path.
Implementation Recommendation: Express appetite as a maximum hot-wallet exposure per asset/chain with automated sweep enforcement and breach escalation to the CRO.
Evidence Required: Board-approved appetite statement; daily hot-exposure vs cap report

Control Objective: Suppliers are known and prioritised by criticality (extended here to critical public software infrastructure).
Relevance to This Incident: The intrusion depended on public package/tooling infrastructure (Homebrew-delivered tools) that sits outside conventional procurement yet is mission-critical.
Implementation Recommendation: Inventory critical developer-tooling dependencies, assign owners, and subject them to the same risk treatment as contracted suppliers.
Evidence Required: Tooling dependency inventory with criticality ratings and owners

Control Objective: Identities and credentials are managed throughout their lifecycle.
Relevance to This Incident: A standing deployment token on a laptop and credentials replayed across machines were central mechanics of the intrusion.
Implementation Recommendation: Short-lived, device-bound credentials; standing endpoint tokens prohibited and continuously scanned for.
Evidence Required: Credential inventory showing zero standing endpoint tokens; token-scan reports
Control Owner: Head of Identity and Access Management

Control Objective: Access permissions, entitlements and authorisations are defined, managed, enforced and reviewed.
Relevance to This Incident: Engineer A's deployment entitlement was exercisable from Engineer C's machine, indicating permissions bound to the person-secret, not the device and context.
Implementation Recommendation: Bind privileged entitlements to device identity and approval context; review wallet-adjacent entitlements monthly.
Evidence Required: Entitlement review records; device-binding configuration evidence
Control Owner: Head of Identity and Access Management

Control Objective: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorised logical access and usage.
Relevance to This Incident: A traversable path existed from corporate endpoints, via internal AI tooling, to the production signing service.
Implementation Recommendation: Signing enclave with a single brokered access path; deny-by-default between corporate and signing zones.
Evidence Required: Network path inventory to the enclave; segmentation test report

Control Objective: Personnel activity and technology are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
Relevance to This Incident: Delegations and re-sweeps proceeded for hours; the operator's detection time is undisclosed while external observers reported within minutes.
Implementation Recommendation: Monitor signing outputs, delegation state and treasury-wallet behaviour with paging thresholds and governed detection metrics.
Evidence Required: Alerting configuration for delegation events; time-to-detect exercise results

Control Objective: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet defined incident criteria.
Relevance to This Incident: Revocation of delegated signing authority had to be improvised; pre-set declaration and escalation criteria for signing anomalies are not evidenced.
Implementation Recommendation: Define signing-anomaly incident criteria with pre-delegated halt and revocation authority.
Evidence Required: Incident criteria document; delegation of authority records; drill logs

Control Objective: Access is limited to the minimum necessary for assigned duties.
Relevance to This Incident: A developer endpoint held a token with container deployment permissions usable toward the signing estate.
Implementation Recommendation: Remove standing deployment rights from endpoints; just-in-time elevation against an approved change/task.
Evidence Required: Access reviews; JIT elevation logs
Control Owner: Head of Identity and Access Management

Control Objective: The system enforces approved authorisations for logical access.
Relevance to This Incident: The signing service enforced caller authorisation but not transaction legitimacy: signatures were produced outside the withdrawal process.
Implementation Recommendation: Require the signing service to verify an approved-withdrawal reference before enforcing any signature request.
Evidence Required: Signing-service policy configuration; negative test results (unreferenced requests rejected)

Control Objective: External and internal boundaries are monitored and controlled; subsystems are separated.
Relevance to This Incident: Corporate-to-signing reachability turned a workstation compromise into a signing compromise across 10-11 chains.
Implementation Recommendation: Dedicated signing enclave; brokered, dual-controlled transit; internal AI tools treated as separate security zones/identities.
Evidence Required: Boundary rule sets; zone architecture diagrams; penetration test report

Control Reference: SI-7 Software, Firmware and Information Integrity (with SSDF PS.2, SP 800-218)
Control Objective: Integrity verification of software and information is performed; release integrity is verifiable.
Relevance to This Incident: A tampered installer and a replaced pyenv component both defeated install-time trust; SSDF PS.2-style release-integrity verification is the direct countermeasure.
Implementation Recommendation: Signature/hash verification at install from a managed catalogue; continuous integrity monitoring of toolchain paths.
Evidence Required: Catalogue verification logs; integrity-monitoring alert records

Control Objective: Information system components are signed and signatures verified before installation/use.
Relevance to This Incident: The June installer was tampered; nothing in the record shows signature verification would have been enforced on a wallet-team workstation.
Implementation Recommendation: Enforce signed-component verification for all developer tooling; block unsigned installers at the endpoint.
Evidence Required: Endpoint policy configuration; blocked-install test evidence

Control Objective: The provenance of system components is tracked and verified.
Relevance to This Incident: The malicious component arrived inside an otherwise legitimate tool (pyenv via Homebrew paths) - a provenance failure within an approved tool.
Implementation Recommendation: Maintain component-level provenance for toolchain packages from a managed mirror; alert on out-of-band component changes.
Evidence Required: Mirror provenance records; component change alerts

Control Objective: The system is monitored to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks.
Relevance to This Incident: No evidenced monitoring fired on a treasury wallet acquiring an EIP-7702 delegation - the single most anomalous event of the intrusion.
Implementation Recommendation: On-chain and off-chain monitoring of signing/delegation events with immediate paging (per TRM guidance).
Evidence Required: Monitoring use-case catalogue; alert test evidence

Control Objective: Incidents are handled with implemented capabilities including preparation, detection, analysis, containment and recovery.
Relevance to This Incident: Containment required designing a revocation procedure mid-incident; preparation for the signing-compromise scenario is the evidenced gap.
Implementation Recommendation: Scenario-specific playbooks for signing compromise, including rehearsed revocation, with defined decision rights.
Evidence Required: Playbook; exercise after-action reports

Control Reference: A.5.21 Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
Control Objective: ICT supply chain risks are identified, assessed and managed.
Relevance to This Incident: Developer tooling obtained from public sources was the initial-access vector twice in four months.
Implementation Recommendation: Extend ICT supply-chain risk management to developer tooling and package infrastructure; verified internal mirror.
Evidence Required: Supply-chain risk register extract for tooling; mirror usage metrics

Control Objective: Privileged access is restricted, controlled and monitored.
Relevance to This Incident: Standing deployment permissions and reusable credentials underpinned lateral movement.
Implementation Recommendation: Privileged access via brokered, time-bound elevation only; standing rights removed and attested.
Evidence Required: Privileged access register; elevation logs
Control Owner: Head of Identity and Access Management

Control Objective: Technical measures protect against malware, supported by user awareness.
Relevance to This Incident: Malware characterised by Binance as zero-day evaded endpoint tools; awareness layer faced a CSO-described, rehearsed TTP.
Implementation Recommendation: Layered malware defence: behavioural EDR, hardened workstations for privileged roles, and scenario-specific staff briefings.
Evidence Required: EDR coverage reports; briefing completion records

Control Objective: Networks, systems and applications are monitored for anomalous behaviour.
Relevance to This Incident: Anomalous signing and delegation behaviour was not demonstrably detected internally within a governed timeframe.
Implementation Recommendation: Define monitored anomalous behaviours to include delegation state changes on treasury wallets; review monitoring effectiveness monthly.
Evidence Required: Monitoring scope document; monthly effectiveness review minutes

Control Objective: Networks are segregated according to information security requirements.
Relevance to This Incident: Segregation between the corporate estate and the signing service did not prevent traversal with stolen credentials.
Implementation Recommendation: Segregate the signing environment; brokered transit only; test segregation independently at least annually.
Evidence Required: Network segregation design; independent test report

Control Reference: A.5.26 Response to information security incidents
Control Objective: Incidents are responded to in accordance with documented procedures.
Relevance to This Incident: Response was energetic but partly improvised (revocation) and disclosure was later restated (coverage figure, intrusion scope).
Implementation Recommendation: Documented, exercised response procedures covering signing compromise, revocation and disclosure control.
Evidence Required: Response procedures; exercise records; disclosure sign-off log

Control Objective: IT-related risk is identified, assessed and reduced to acceptable levels within appetite.
Relevance to This Incident: The register-level risks (hot-wallet concentration, signing path) materialised jointly; appetite governance is the COBIT home for both.
Implementation Recommendation: Maintain this register as a living artefact with appetite-linked KRIs reported to the risk committee.
Evidence Required: Risk register review minutes; KRI dashboard

Control Objective: An information security management system is established and maintained.
Relevance to This Incident: Signing-authority policy - the control that failed most literally - belongs inside a managed security system with named ownership.
Implementation Recommendation: Assign signing-authority policy to a named owner within the ISMS, with annual review and exception reporting.
Evidence Required: ISMS scope and policy register; exception log

Control Objective: Security services protect enterprise information and technology assets in operation.
Relevance to This Incident: Endpoint, network and detection services are where M1-M3 and M6 were won or lost operationally.
Implementation Recommendation: Operate detection and endpoint services against defined service levels, including time-to-detect for signing anomalies.
Evidence Required: Security services SLA reports

Control Objective: Continuity capabilities maintain operations through disruptive events.
Relevance to This Incident: Withdrawal suspension and phased reopening were a continuity event executed without published criteria or a full-restoration date.
Implementation Recommendation: Document reopening criteria tied to control verification; exercise liquidity-and-continuity scenarios.
Evidence Required: Continuity plan; exercise reports; reopening decision records

Control Reference: MEA03 Managed Compliance with External Requirements
Control Objective: Compliance with external requirements is identified, assessed and reported.
Relevance to This Incident: Reuters documents a fragmented landscape - prescriptive (NYDFS) to non-prescriptive (money-transmitter) regimes - with expectations likely to harden.
Implementation Recommendation: Jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction requirements and notification matrix, tested; adopt the strictest standard as the global baseline.
Evidence Required: Compliance matrix; notification test results

Control Objective: Only authorised software is permitted to execute/install.
Relevance to This Incident: A tampered installer and a trojanised toolchain component both executed on engineering endpoints.
Implementation Recommendation: Technical allow-listing for developer tooling on engineering estates, fed from the verified catalogue.
Evidence Required: Allow-list policy; blocked-install logs

Control Reference: Safeguard 10.1 Deploy and Maintain Anti-Malware Software
Control Objective: Anti-malware is deployed and maintained on all enterprise assets.
Relevance to This Incident: Baseline safeguard whose limits the incident also demonstrates: necessary, not sufficient, against unidentified malware - hence pairing with segmentation and signing controls.
Implementation Recommendation: Maintain anti-malware/EDR universally; measure behavioural-detection outcomes, not just deployment.
Evidence Required: Deployment coverage report; detection test results

Control Reference: Safeguard 6.8 Define and Maintain Role-Based Access Control
Control Objective: Access is granted on role-based definitions and reviewed.
Relevance to This Incident: Deployment entitlements were exercisable cross-machine, indicating role definitions not bound to device/context.
Implementation Recommendation: Role definitions for wallet-adjacent entitlements bound to device and approval context; monthly review.
Evidence Required: RBAC definitions; review sign-offs
Control Owner: Head of Identity and Access Management

Control Objective: Audit logs are reviewed regularly for anomalies.
Relevance to This Incident: Regular review discipline supports - but does not replace - real-time alerting on delegation and signing events.
Implementation Recommendation: Include signing-service and delegation logs in the reviewed set with documented review cadence.
Evidence Required: Log review records; sampled alert dispositions

Control Objective: Access to resources is restricted to authorised users and processes (applied by analogy; no attestation asserted).
Relevance to This Incident: Counterparties will test custodial platforms against this criterion; the credential/token mechanics map directly onto it.
Implementation Recommendation: Meet CC6.1-grade logical access discipline for the signing estate, evidenced to counterparty due-diligence standard.
Evidence Required: Access control evidence pack
Control Owner: Head of Identity and Access Management

Control Objective: Operations are monitored to detect anomalies and deviations (applied by analogy).
Relevance to This Incident: The undisclosed detection time is the assurance gap this criterion exists to close.
Implementation Recommendation: Operate and evidence anomaly detection over signing operations with reported metrics.
Evidence Required: Detection metrics pack; incident timeline disclosures

Control Objective: The entity responds to identified security incidents per defined procedures (applied by analogy).
Relevance to This Incident: Revocation improvisation and disclosure restatements are the response-quality questions a CC7.4 lens raises.
Implementation Recommendation: Defined, exercised incident procedures including revocation and disclosure control.
Evidence Required: Procedure documents; exercise evidence
